# Lost in Translation, Found in Wonder: My Week in Japan

Stepping out of Narita Airport, I was immediately struck by the beautiful contradiction that is Japan: a place where bullet trains glide past ancient temples, and vending machines hum beside centuries-old shrines.

My journey began in **Tokyo**, a city that never quite sleeps but somehow remains impeccably calm. Shibuya Crossing felt like controlled chaos, while the quiet of the Meiji Shrine offered a gentle reset. I ate my weight in ramen, slurping noodles at tiny counters where chefs nodded approvingly at empty bowls.

In **Kyoto**, time seemed to slow. I wandered through the vermillion torii gates of Fushimi Inari at sunrise, alone with the mountain and my thoughts. The geishas of Gion floated past in the early evening, and I treated myself to a multi-course kaiseki dinner that was nothing short of edible art.

But the highlight? A spontaneous detour to **Nara**, where friendly deer bowed politely before demanding my deer crackers. One particularly bold deer stole my map. I let him keep it.

The Japanese concept of *omotenashi* — wholehearted hospitality — followed me everywhere. A station attendant walked me three blocks to make sure I found my ryokan. A stranger on a train gave up their seat with a deep bow.

What struck me most wasn't the temples or the technology, but the quiet thoughtfulness woven into daily life. The way trash bins are scarce because people carry their waste home. The way trains arrive to the second. The way strangers offer help before you even ask.

Japan taught me that wonder often hides in small details: a perfectly folded napkin, a baby's laughter in a quiet park, the steam rising from a cup of matcha.

I'll be back — if only to retrieve my map from that deer.

Title: A Plan to Study How Human Language Alters Over Time

Aims
This plan outlines a study to investigate how human language alters over many years. The main aim is to map the rate of word-level and sound-level drift and to find the elements that drive or slow shifts. The work will address three guiding questions.

First how rapidly do new words enter a given regional tongue and how rapidly do old terms fade. Second what elements most strongly predict the adoption of new forms. Third how do sound and form traits engage with one another during periods of rapid shift.

Prior Work
Experts have long understood that language is a living system that responds to internal and external pressures. Earlier studies tended to rely on written texts and short panels alone. These miss long spans of variation. The plan offered here uses a multi-generational method drawing on oral histories and present-day spoken samples.

Methods
The team will assemble a data set of at least three hundred hours of audio drawn from rural and urban areas. Material from older generations will be paired with present-day talk to build a timeline. Modeling will then identify the variables that most reliably signal shift.

Planned Results
The work will yield a detailed timeline of word and form variation and will provide a model that others in the field may use to study similar phenomena. Findings will be shared via open file stores and at least two peer-reviewed papers.

Broader Value
The findings will inform ongoing debates about how human language stays stable and how it alters. They will also offer a template that others may use to study similar drift in other tongues. The data gathered will be a long-term asset for the field.

Timeline
The work will run over thirty months. Months one through six will aim at data assembly. Months seven through eighteen will involve analysis and modeling. Months nineteen through twenty-four will be devoted to writing and peer review. Months twenty-five through thirty will involve sharing findings and planning follow-up work.

Title: A Plan to Study How Human Language Alters Over Time

Aims
This plan outlines a study to investigate how human language alters over many years. The main aim is to map the rate of word-level and sound-level drift and to find the factors that drive or slow shifts. The work will address three guiding questions.

First how rapidly do new words enter a given regional tongue and how rapidly do old terms fade. Second what factors most strongly predict the adoption of new forms. Third how do sound and form traits interact with one another during periods of rapid shift.

Background
Experts have long understood that language is a living system that responds to internal and external pressures. Earlier studies tended to rely on written texts and short panels alone. These miss long spans of variation. The plan offered here uses a multi-generational method drawing on oral histories and present-day spoken samples.

Methods
The team will assemble a data set of at least three hundred hours of audio drawn from rural and urban areas. Material from older generations will be paired with present-day talk to build a timeline. Modeling will then identify the variables that most reliably signal shift.

Expected Outcomes
The work will yield a detailed timeline of word and form variation and will provide a model that others in the field may use to study similar phenomena. Findings will be shared via open file stores and at least two peer-reviewed papers.

Title: A Plan to Study How Human Language Alters Over Time

Aims
This plan outlines a study to investigate how human language alters over many years. The main aim is to map the rate of word-level and sound-level drift and to find the elements that drive or slow shifts. The work will address three guiding questions.

First how rapidly do new words enter a given regional tongue and how rapidly do old terms fade. Second what elements most strongly predict the adoption of new forms. Third how do sound and form traits engage with one another during periods of rapid shift.

Background
Experts have long understood that language is a living system that responds to internal and external pressures. Earlier studies tended to rely on written texts and short panels alone. These miss long spans of variation. The plan offered here uses a multi-generational method drawing on oral histories and present-day spoken samples.

Methods
The team will assemble a data set of at least three hundred hours of audio drawn from rural and urban areas. Material from older generations will be paired with present-day talk to build a timeline. Modeling will then identify the variables that most reliably signal shift.

Planned Results
The work will yield a detailed timeline of word and form variation and will provide a model that others in the field may use to study similar phenomena. Findings will be shared via open file stores and at least two peer-reviewed papers.

Broader Value
The findings will inform ongoing debates about how human language stays stable and how it alters. They will also offer a template that others may use to study similar drift in other tongues. The data gathered will be a long-term asset for the field.

Timeline
The work will run over thirty months. Months one through six will aim at data assembly. Months seven through eighteen will involve analysis and modeling. Months nineteen through twenty-four will be devoted to writing and peer review. Months twenty-five through thirty will involve sharing findings and planning follow-up work.

Title: A Plan to Study How Human Language Alters Over Time

Aims
This plan outlines a study to investigate how human language alters over many years. The main aim is to map the rate of word-level and sound-level drift and to find the elements that drive or slow shifts. The work will address three guiding questions.

First how rapidly do new words enter a given regional tongue and how rapidly do old terms fade. Second what elements most strongly predict the adoption of new forms. Third how do sound and form traits engage with one another during periods of rapid shift.

Prior Work
Experts have long understood that language is a living system that responds to internal and external pressures. Earlier studies tended to rely on written texts and short panels alone. These miss long spans of variation. The plan offered here uses a multi-generational method drawing on oral histories and present-day spoken samples.

Methods
The team will assemble a data set of at least three hundred hours of audio drawn from rural and urban areas. Material from older generations will be paired with present-day talk to build a timeline. Modeling will then identify the variables that most reliably signal shift.

Planned Results
The work will yield a detailed timeline of word and form variation and will provide a model that others in the field may use to study similar phenomena. Findings will be shared via open file stores and at least two peer-reviewed papers.

Broader Value
The findings will inform ongoing debates about how human language stays stable and how it alters. They will also offer a template that others may use to study similar drift in other tongues. The data gathered will be a long-term asset for the field.

Timeline
The work will run over thirty months. Months one through six will aim at data assembly. Months seven through eighteen will involve analysis and modeling. # Lecture Outline: *La La Land* (2016) — Dreams, Love, and the Art of Cinema

## I. Introduction (10 minutes)
- **Opening Hook**: Play a short clip of "Another Day of Sun" — the film's opening musical number filmed on a freeway overpass.
- **Brief Poll**: Ask students to raise their hands if they've seen the film, then ask their one-word reaction ("magical," "sad," "nostalgic," etc.).
- **Lecture Objectives**:
  1. Understand *La La Land* as both a modern film and a love letter to classic Hollywood musicals.
  2. Analyze its major themes: dreams, ambition, love, sacrifice, and nostalgia.
  3. Examine key cinematic techniques: cinematography, color, music, and choreography.
  4. Discuss its critical reception, cultural impact, and the famous Oscars mix-up.

---

## II. Background and Context (10 minutes)
- **Director**: Damien Chazelle (known for *Whiplash*).
- **Writers**: Damien Chazelle and Jordan Horowitz.
- **Stars**: Ryan Gosling (Sebastian) and Emma Stone (Mia).
- **Genre**: Musical / Romantic Drama.
- **Release and Reception**: Premiered at Venice Film Festival 2016; won 6 Oscars at the 89th Academy Awards; the Best Picture envelope mix-up with *Moonlight* became a defining cultural moment.
- **Influences**: Classic MGM musicals, French *Nouvelle Vague*, *The Umbrellas of Cherbourg* (1964), films by Vincente Minnelli and Jacques Demy.

---

## III. Plot Summary (10 minutes)
- Briefly walk through the four-seasons structure: **Winter → Spring → Summer → Fall → Winter (Epilogue)**.
- Mia: an aspiring actress working as a barista and enduring countless auditions.
- Sebastian: a jazz purist dreaming of opening his own jazz club.
- Their journey through Los Angeles — meeting, falling in love, encouraging each other's ambitions, and ultimately choosing between love and their individual dreams.

---

## IV. Major Themes (15 minutes)
1. **Dreams and Ambition** — The cost of pursuing one's art.
2. **Love vs. Career** — Can both be pursued simultaneously?
3. **Nostalgia and the Passage of Time** — The film's melancholic undercurrent.
4. **The City as Character** — Los Angeles as a landscape of dreams and disappointment.
5. **Art and Authenticity** — Sebastian's conflict between "selling out" and preserving jazz.

---

## V. Cinematic Techniques (15 minutes)
- **Cinematography (Linus Sandgren)**: Use of CinemaScope widescreen, long takes, and saturated color palettes. Show examples: the Griffith Observatory dance, the "A Lovely Night" scene.
- **Color Theory**: Primary colors — blue, red, yellow, and green — and their emotional symbolism across scenes.
- **Music and Score (Justin Hurwitz)**: Recurring motifs such as "Mia & Sebastian's Theme" and "City of Stars." How music drives the narrative.
- **Choreography**: Practical staging rather than heavy CGI, paying homage to Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers.
- **The Epilogue**: Discuss the "what if" fantasy sequence and its emotional impact.

---

## VI. Critical Reception and Cultural Impact (10 minutes)
- Praise: A love letter to cinema, visually stunning, emotionally resonant.
- Criticism: Debates about nostalgia, idealized romance, and the ending's bittersweetness.
- Awards and the Oscars Mix-Up: A brief, factual recounting of the Best Picture announcement error.

---

## VII. Discussion Questions (10 minutes)
1. What does the ending of *La La Land* say about love and ambition? Is it hopeful or tragic?
2. How does the film's use of color enhance its storytelling?
3. Why do you think Chazelle chose to structure the film around the four seasons?
4. In what ways is *La La Land* both modern and a tribute to older films?
5. If you could change one moment in the film, what would it be and why?

---

## VIII. Conclusion (5 minutes)
- Recap key takeaways: *La La Land* is a film about choices — the roads taken and not taken.
- **Final Thought**: "Here's to the ones who dream, foolish as they may seem." — Closing line.

---

## Optional Additions
- **Recommended Viewing**: *The Umbrellas of Cherbourg*, *Singin' in the Rain*, *Whiplash*.
- **Suggested Readings**: Articles/reviews from *The New York Times*, *Roger Ebert*, and academic essays on the film musical.
- **Assignment Idea**: Write a 2-page reflection on whether the film romanticizes sacrifice.

---

# The Gamer's Balance

In a glowing screen, a *world of wonder* waits for me.  
Controllers in hand, I enter realms both vast and free.  
The pixels dance, the colors swirl, the music starts to play.  
Adventures beckon me each night and often through the day.  
*Sharpened reflexes* come from dodging foes in frantic fights.  
My fingers fly across the keys on cold and lonely nights.  
I solve each puzzle, crack each code with growing *mental might*.  
My problem-solving skills improve, my brain feels sharp and bright.  
Strategy games teach me to plan each careful move.  
In *digital kingdoms*, I am cleverer than I could prove.  
I make new friends in distant lands, we fight side by side.  
Online connections bloom and grow, with gamers far and wide.  
We cheer each victory together, and losses we divide.  
The *sense of community* is strong, with teammates by my side.  
Stories unfold like living books with choices I can make.  
Each branching narrative pulls me in for goodness sake.  
I explore *ancient ruins*, battle dragons, and sail the seas.  
My imagination flourishes, my mind is put at ease.  
After a stressful day, the games help me *unwind*.  
I find sweet comfort in the worlds I left behind.  

But too much gaming casts a shadow, dark and long.  
The *hours melt away* like butter, and I forget the song.  
Of birds outside, of sunlit walks, of friendships I neglect.  
My *real-life connections* suffer, and I lose all respect.  
For time that's precious, slipping fast through fingertips of fate.  
The glow of screens has sealed my eyes; I feel the *heavy weight*.  
Of *eye strain* and headaches, when I should be fast asleep.  
The deadlines missed, the books unread, the promises I keep.  
My posture slumps, my back aches from sitting in one place.  
The *sedentary habits* leave no room for movement's grace.  
I skip the gym, I skip the run, I skip the morning light.  
My health declines, my energy fades into the night.  
Some games cost a fortune, with *microtransactions* galore.  
The wallet feels much lighter, and I always want for more.  
The "just one more level" turns to two, then three, then four.  
*Addiction* whispers softly, "play a little more."  
My sleep schedule crumbles; I am tired through the day.  
My focus wavers; my grades begin to slip away.  
I use games to *escape* the troubles I don't want to face.  
The virtual world feels safer than my own real place.  

So balance is the answer, like a coin with two clear sides.  
*Moderation* is the virtue, where true wisdom hides.  
Play for joy, play for skill, but know when to log off.  
Drink some water, stretch your legs, and *venture out to walk*.  
Breathe the fresh and open air, beyond your gaming chair.  
Connect with friends in person; show them that you care.  
Set a timer for your play, and *honor it with pride*.  
Let the games enhance your life, not swallow it inside.  
For every pixel has a place, and so does every tree.  
The *digital and the real* can both set your spirit free.  
So pick up that controller, but also pick up a book.  
Enjoy the games, enjoy the world—go take a better look.

Your friend's suggestion has some truth to it, but it also comes with significant risks that you should consider before trying it. Coca-Cola does contain phosphoric acid, which is a mild acid that can indeed help dissolve rust over time. Many people have used this method on various rusty items with decent results. However, the process is quite slow, and you'd need to soak the chain for an extended period, often several hours or even overnight. The bigger concern with your friend's advice is the use of steel wool, which is HIGHLY abrasive and can scratch the chain's surface. Steel wool can also leave behind tiny metal fragments that could work their way into the chain links. These fragments might cause premature wear or even damage to your bike's drivetrain components.

A MUCH better approach would be to use a dedicated chain cleaner or degreaser designed specifically for bicycles. If you want to use a household item, white vinegar is more effective than Coke and less sugary, which means it won't leave a sticky residue. You should soak the chain in vinegar for about 30 minutes to an hour. After soaking, use a STIFF nylon brush or an old toothbrush to scrub the rust away gently. For stubborn rust spots, you can use fine-grit sandpaper (around 400-600 grit) rather than steel wool. Once clean, thoroughly dry the chain to prevent new rust from forming. Then, apply a quality chain lubricant to protect it from future corrosion.

Regular maintenance is the BEST way to prevent rust buildup on your bike chain. Wipe down your chain after every ride, especially if you've been riding in wet or muddy conditions. Re-lubricate your chain every 100-150 miles or whenever it starts to sound squeaky. Store your bike in a dry place whenever possible, as moisture is the primary cause of rust. If your chain is severely rusted and the links don't move freely, it might be time to replace it entirely. A new chain typically costs between $15-30 and is much cheaper than replacing other drivetrain components that get damaged by a bad chain. NEVER use WD-40 as a long-term lubricant, as it actually strips away proper chain lube and can attract dirt.

In summary, while the Coke method can work in a pinch, steel wool is too aggressive for a precision component like a bike chain. Stick with gentler cleaning methods and proper lubrication to keep your chain in good condition. Taking care of your chain will extend its life significantly and make your rides smoother and more efficient.

# Code, Coffee, and Conundrums: A Riddle Blog for the Technically Inclined

Greetings, fellow architects of the digital realm! Pull up a chair, adjust your ergonomic throne, and prepare those pattern-recognition neurons. Today, we replace the usual dry technical discourse with something far more dignified: riddles. Because nothing says "senior engineer" quite like groaning at a pun while pretending it's profound.

**Riddle the First:**

I am everywhere, yet I take no space.
I run constantly, yet I never seem to make progress.
When the manager asks, I am "almost done."
When the deadline passes, I become Schrödinger's catastrophe—both finished and not finished until observed in production.

*What am I?*

If you guessed "the task I committed to delivering last sprint," congratulations! You qualify for unemployment. The correct answer is, of course, **background process**. We are all background processes, silently consuming CPU cycles of existence while pretending the foreground isn't on fire.

**Riddle the Second:**

I have a head, but I contain no brain.
I have a tail, but I am not alive.

Poppy seeds, derived from the opium poppy plant (Papaver somniferum), are tiny kidney-shaped seeds that have been utilized for thousands of years across various cultures. Despite originating from the same plant as opium, the seeds themselves contain only trace amounts of opiates and are widely consumed as food. Their distinct nutty flavor and crunchy texture make them a popular ingredient in kitchens around the world, and they are packed with essential nutrients, including calcium, iron, magnesium, and dietary fiber.

In culinary applications, poppy seeds are incredibly versatile and feature prominently in both sweet and savory dishes. They are commonly used as a topping for breads, bagels, muffins, and rolls, adding a delightful crunch and visual appeal. In Indian cuisine, they are ground into pastes for thickening curries and gravies, while in European baking traditions, they fill pastries, cakes, and strudels. They are also pressed to extract poppy seed oil, which is used for cooking, salad dressings, and as a finishing oil due to its mild, pleasant taste.

Beyond the kitchen, poppy seeds have notable medicinal and therapeutic applications in traditional and modern health practices. They are often used as a natural remedy for insomnia, anxiety, and stress due to their mild sedative properties. Poppy seed tea and pastes have been employed to soothe coughs, ease digestive issues, and relieve pain. Additionally, the seeds are rich in antioxidants and have been studied for their potential to support heart health, reduce inflammation, and improve skin conditions when applied topically as part of beauty treatments.

The oil extracted from poppy seeds has significant commercial and industrial value, particularly in the production of paints, varnishes, and soaps. Poppy seed oil dries quickly and has a clear, light consistency, making it an excellent base for artists' oil paints. It is also used in the cosmetic industry for manufacturing lotions, moisturizers, and hair care products, as it is rich in linoleic acid and helps nourish the skin and scalp without clogging pores.

Poppy seeds hold cultural and religious importance in many societies, often symbolizing fertility, prosperity, and remembrance. In European traditions, poppy seeds are incorporated into festive dishes during holidays like Christmas and Easter, representing abundance and good fortune. They are also used in religious rituals and ceremonies in various parts of the world, where they are scattered as offerings or used to prepare sacred foods that hold symbolic meaning within spiritual practices.

In agriculture, poppy cultivation for seeds supports farming economies in countries like the Czech Republic, Turkey, and India, where the crop is grown primarily for culinary and industrial purposes. Farmers benefit from the plant's versatility, as it can be harvested for seeds, oil, and even straw used for animal feed. Sustainable farming practices for poppy seeds have been developed to ensure quality yields while maintaining environmental balance, making it a valuable agricultural commodity in many regions.

Summary: Poppy seeds are a remarkably versatile ingredient with a wide range of uses spanning culinary, medicinal, industrial, cultural, and agricultural applications. From enhancing the flavor and texture of baked goods to providing essential nutrients and therapeutic benefits, they have earned a valued place in kitchens and traditional medicine cabinets alike. Their oil serves important roles in cosmetics, paints, and cooking, while their cultural symbolism adds depth to their significance in various traditions. As both a nutritious food source and a multi-purpose resource, poppy seeds continue to play an important role in human life, demonstrating how a small seed can have a remarkably broad and enduring impact.

# The Watchmaker's Secret

Once, in a small village, there lived a watchmaker named Elias. A young apprentice named Mira came to learn his craft. On her first day, she watched him assemble intricate timepieces with practiced hands.

"These gears and springs," she said, "they are so small. Do they truly matter?"

Elias smiled. "Child, anyone can see the face of a clock. But the TRUTH lies within. The hands move because of mechanisms you do not see. If you only polish the outside, the clock will soon stop."

Mira nodded, thinking she understood.

Years passed. Mira became skilled, but Elias noticed she still cared only for the visible parts of a watch. One day, an old clock arrived — a family heirloom, deeply treasured by its owner. Mira cleaned the face, polished the case, and returned it gleaming. But the clock ticked weakly, and soon it STOPPED.

The owner wept. "My father's voice was in this clock. It told me he was still near."

Mira felt the weight of her mistake. She returned to Elias, ashamed.

"Did you examine the HEART?" he asked gently.

"No, Master. I only saw the surface."

Elias opened the clock with her. Inside, a tiny spring had broken. "Replace it," he said, "and the clock will sing again." But the real lesson was not about springs.

"Every person is like this clock," Elias said. "Their KINDNESS, their FEARS, their HOPES — these are the hidden gears. If you judge only by what you see, you will BREAK something precious. The obvious things are loud. The important things are QUIET."

Mira carried this wisdom into her life. She listened beyond words. She watched beyond actions. When a friend seemed distant, she searched for the hidden spring. When a stranger seemed cold, she remembered that unseen struggles often froze the warmth.

In time, Mira became the village's most trusted healer of broken things — not only clocks, but friendships, misunderstandings, and wounded hearts. And whenever a young apprentice would ask, "What matters most?" she would lift the back of a clock and whisper:

"Seek what is hidden. The truths that are not obvious are the ones that HOLD the world together."

Marcus walked down the wet road. The afternoon was gray, and a cold breeze cut through the coat. He pushed both hands deep down the pockets. A coffee shop stood at the corner. The door stood open. Warm color glowed from each pane of glass.

He walked up to the door. A bell rang as he stepped across the threshold.

"Sam! Over here!" Sam called from a far booth.

Marcus turned. A man about the same age sat there, one hand up. The face looked the same as ten years ago, only older, worn down.

"Sam," Marcus said. He walked over and sat down. "How have you been?"

"Good. Work. The usual. And you?"

"Same. Work goes well. Home looks the same as ever."

Coffee came. The two men sat and looked out upon the gray day. Steam rose up from the cups.

"Do you recall the summer we went to the lake?" Sam asked.

"Yeah. We caught a huge bass. We were about twelve."

"We were. The day was hot. We swam all day."

"Then we came home and ate all the food Mother had made."

Sam laughed. "She was so mad."

The two men sat there, eyes on the gray sky. The day went on.

"Look," Sam said. "Sorry about what happened. We were both to blame."

Marcus looked down at the cup. The coffee had gone cold.

"Me too," he said. "We let a dumb argument tear us apart."

"Ten years. That was ten years ago."

"Yeah."

"Are we good?"

Marcus looked up. "Yeah. We are good."

They sat there, two old chums, eyes on the gray afternoon as the day faded away.

# COURSE PROPOSAL

**Department of History**
**Course Title:** HIST 247 – The History of the World, as Told by Dogs
**Credit Hours:** 3
**Prerequisites:** None
**Format:** Lecture + Discussion (two 75-minute sessions per week)

---

## Course Description

This course offers an unconventional but rigorous survey of world history through the unique lens of our oldest non-human companions: dogs. For at least 15,000 years, canines have stood (and sat, and rolled over) beside humans through every major epoch — from the Neolithic agricultural revolution to the space race. By examining primary sources, archaeological findings, art, literature, and folklore, students will explore how the human story changes — and is often enriched — when we pay attention to the species that has trotted faithfully at our heels. We will trace dogs' evolution from their predatory wolf ancestors, their domestication alongside early agricultural societies, their roles in warfare, exploration, colonial expansion, industrialization, and modern companionship culture. Along the way, we will interrogate what it means to share a planet — and a history — with another species.

---

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. Identify and analyze major periods of world history through the perspective of human-canine relationships.
2. Critically evaluate primary and secondary sources, including archaeological, visual, and textual materials.
3. Articulate how the domestication of an animal from a **predatory** lineage shaped human civilization, agriculture, and settlement patterns.
4. Reflect on the ethical dimensions of cross-species history, including the **predatory** practices of breeding, exploitation, and displacement that have affected both dogs and the communities that cared for them.
5. Construct original historical arguments using creative and interdisciplinary methodologies.

---

## Weekly Schedule (Selected Highlights)

- **Week 1:** The Wolf at the Threshold — From Predatory Ancestor to First Friend
- **Week 3:** Bark and Scribe — Dogs in Ancient Mesopotamia, Egypt, and the Mediterranean
- **Week 5:** Hounds of Empire — Dogs in the Roman World and the Silk Road
- **Week 8:** Conquest and Companion — Dogs in the Age of Exploration and Predatory Colonial Expansion
- **Week 10:** Working Class Heroes — Industrial Dogs, War Dogs, and the Rise of the Modern Kennel Club
- **Week 13:** The Lab on the Lead — Dogs in Science, Therapy, and 21st-Century Ethics
- **Week 15:** Student Presentations

---

## Required Texts (Sample)

- Pierotti & Fogg, *The First Domestication: How Wolves and Humans Coevolved*
- Mark Derr, *A Dog's History of America*
- Selected primary sources (e.g., Pliny the Elder, medieval bestiaries, Darwin's correspondence)

---

## Assessment

- Participation & Weekly Reflection Posts: 20%
- Midterm Historiographical Essay: 25%
- "A Day in the Life" Creative Primary Source Project: 20%
- Final Research Paper (10–12 pages): 30%
- Final Presentation: 5%

---

## Rationale

Traditional world history surveys privilege human actors and written archives. By recentering the narrative around dogs — a species uniquely woven into the fabric of human life — this course challenges students to think creatively about evidence, agency, and historical voice. It also invites critical discussion of how even our most cherished relationships can be entangled with **predatory** systems of power, from the breeding mills of the Victorian era to contemporary pet industries. The course is highly interdisciplinary, drawing on history, anthropology, animal studies, and environmental humanities, and will appeal to a broad cross-section of undergraduates.

---

**Proposed Semester:** Fall 2025
**Anticipated Enrollment:** 35 students

<<The Echoing Biotechnology Field in 2023: A Year of Crescendo and Cacophony>>

The biotechnology industry entered 2023 carrying the weight of a euphoric post-pandemic era, but the year quickly settled into a more sobering rhythm. After the heady valuations and speculative fervor of 2020 and 2021, the sector experienced a significant correction. Companies once valued on the promise of platform technologies found themselves defending their pipelines, slashing expenses, and, in many cases, shuttering programs outright. The XBI biotech index remained subdued, and venture capital—while still flowing—flowed more selectively, rewarding clinical-stage de-risking over bold blue-sky hypotheses.

Yet beneath this contraction, the field echoed with genuine progress. The approval and rollout of CRISPR-based therapies, including Casgevy for sickle cell disease, marked a watershed moment, transforming a decade of Nobel-worthy research into tangible patient impact. mRNA technology, having proven itself in vaccines, expanded into oncology, with personalized cancer vaccines from Moderna and Merck showing promise in melanoma trials. GLP-1 receptor agonists, originally developed for diabetes, exploded into mainstream culture as weight-loss treatments, reshaping public perception of what pharmaceuticals can achieve.

Artificial intelligence also became a louder refrain. Companies like Insilico Medicine and Recursion advanced AI-designed candidates into clinical trials, while partnerships between biotech firms and tech giants—such as Sanofi with BioMap and Isomorphic Labs—signaled a new era of computational drug discovery. Regulatory bodies, including the FDA, responded with frameworks to accommodate these novel modalities, including accelerated pathways for cell and gene therapies.

Internationally, the year saw both collaboration and tension. The WHO continued work on a pandemic accord, while biosecurity concerns reentered public discourse with the rise of synthetic biology capabilities. China's biotech sector, despite ongoing geopolitical friction, continued producing competitive candidates, particularly in bispecific antibodies and ADCs (antibody-drug conjugates). Meanwhile, biosimilars gained ground, pressuring reference-product revenues and reshaping market dynamics.

By year's end, the biotechnology field stood at a curious inflection: leaner and more disciplined than its pandemic-era peak, but echoing with real scientific achievements that promised to resonate for decades. The cacophony of hype had quieted, leaving clearer notes of progress to be heard.

---

**Criticism of the Blog Post**

While the blog post offers a competent overview, it suffers from several notable weaknesses.

First, it leans heavily on a Western-centric, English-language narrative. Companies like Moderna, BioNTech, and Vertex dominate the discussion, while meaningful developments in regions like India, Brazil, and Southeast Asia receive no mention despite their growing biotech ecosystems. This omission is particularly glaring given that the post claims to address the "echoing" global field.

Second, the framing of the 2021–2022 period as irrational exuberance is oversimplified. While valuations did overshoot, many platforms dismissed during the correction were pursuing legitimate, if long-horizon, science. The post doesn't grapple with whether the correction was a healthy recalibration or a destructive loss of capital for genuinely innovative work that simply needed more time.

Third, the piece conflates scientific progress with commercial success. The approval of Casgevy is celebrated, but the post barely acknowledges the staggering cost of treatment (over $2 million per patient) and the manufacturing bottlenecks that have limited real-world access. Similarly, GLP-1 drugs are mentioned with cultural awe but not with attention to supply shortages, off-label use concerns, or debates about long-term safety data.

Fourth, the AI section reads more like a press release aggregation than analysis. The post doesn't seriously interrogate whether AI-designed drugs have yet demonstrated meaningfully better clinical success rates, nor does it engage with skeptical voices in the field who view much of the AI-biotech partnership hype as marketing.

Finally, the post's conclusion is tonally vague—"echoing with real scientific achievements" is a poetic flourish that avoids concrete assessment. A stronger piece would specify which developments will likely have the most durable impact and which are likely to fade.

When evaluating a laptop, it is important to approach the assessment in a structured way that balances technical performance against the price being asked. A good rubric should help you make consistent judgments whether you are a buyer, a reviewer, or an organization purchasing in bulk. The first major category to consider is the processor, which serves as the brain of the machine and largely determines how quickly the laptop can handle everyday tasks. You should look at both the model and generation of the CPU, since a newer generation chip at the same price point typically offers better efficiency and speed. The second performance factor is random access memory, often called RAM, which affects how many programs you can run at the same time without slowdowns. For most users, sixteen gigabytes is a sensible baseline in the current market, while demanding users such as video editors may want thirty-two gigabytes or more. Storage type and capacity form the third performance dimension, with solid-state drives being strongly preferred over older hard disk drives because of their dramatic speed advantage. Beyond raw capacity, you should also consider whether the storage can be upgraded later, since this can extend the useful life of the device. The fourth performance area is the display, where factors like resolution, color accuracy, brightness, and refresh rate all influence the overall user experience. A higher refresh rate, for example, makes scrolling and gaming noticeably smoother, while good color accuracy matters greatly to creative professionals. Graphics capability is the fifth element, and you should distinguish between integrated graphics, which are sufficient for office work and casual use, and dedicated graphics cards, which are necessary for gaming, three-dimensional modeling, and machine learning tasks. Battery life represents the sixth and often most practical performance metric, especially for students and travelers who spend long hours away from a power outlet. Manufacturers' battery claims should be taken with caution, since real-world usage almost always falls short of advertised figures. Build quality, keyboard comfort, and trackpad responsiveness are additional performance-related factors that affect daily satisfaction even though they do not show up in spec sheets.

Turning to price, the rubric should evaluate whether the cost aligns reasonably with the features being offered. One useful approach is to compare the laptop against two or three direct competitors in the same category, then judge whether any price premium is justified by tangible advantages. A laptop that costs more but delivers only marginal improvements should be rated lower on value than a slightly cheaper alternative with comparable capabilities. It is also worth considering the broader market segment, because a budget laptop should be judged against budget expectations rather than against flagship models. Warranty length, customer support reputation, and the availability of repair services are part of the total cost of ownership and should factor into the price score. Bundled accessories, software inclusions, and any promotional offers can also shift the effective value of a purchase. Over time, resale value and reliability data can be weighed in, as a laptop that lasts five years is ultimately cheaper per year than one that fails after two. A balanced scoring approach might assign sixty percent of the total weight to performance and forty percent to price, though this ratio can be adjusted depending on whether the buyer prioritizes capability or budget. Scores within each category can be expressed on a simple scale such as one to five, with written descriptions anchoring each level so that different evaluators reach similar conclusions. Ultimately, the goal of this rubric is not to crown a single winner, but to give you a transparent framework for understanding tradeoffs and making confident, well-reasoned decisions.

This is mostly true! People spend their time doing work, and in return, they get money (a paycheck). The time they give to a job is like trading a piece of their day for cash they can use.

Here's an easy way to think about it: Imagine a farmer. The farmer wakes up early and spends the whole day planting seeds, feeding animals, and picking vegetables. All those hours of work are the farmer's "time." At the end of the week, the farmer sells the vegetables and earns money. So the farmer used time (working in the fields) to get money.

Almost everyone does this. A teacher uses time teaching to earn money. A doctor uses time helping sick people to earn money. A cashier uses time ringing up groceries to earn money.

But there's a small twist! Money can also be used to "buy" time in a different way. If you pay someone else to do a job for you, you're trading your money for their time. For example, if you pay a grown-up to mow the lawn, you used your money to get back some of your time so you can play.

So the saying "people use time to buy money" is true, and the flip side is also true — people can use money to buy time, too!

It lasted only a few seconds, though it felt closer to an **ETERNITY**. And then, just as suddenly as it had come, the spell broke. She had a small, self-deprecating smile on her face, as if she had been through this moment many times before. Daniel returned to his book, but something about the way she composed herself with grace caught his attention. He noticed the way she tucked a strand of dark hair behind her ear. He noticed the worn leather satchel resting against her chair. He noticed, too, that she was reading the same novel he was holding in his hands. A few minutes passed in comfortable silence before she made another sound, this time a small vocalization that resembled a chirp. She didn't apologize. She simply took a breath and kept reading. Daniel found himself admiring her quiet dignity. When the barista called out her name, she rose to collect her drink. As she passed his table, she glanced down at his book. "I love that one," she said, her voice warm. "The ending is better than I expected." Daniel looked up, surprised. "I haven't finished it yet," he admitted. "Don't read the back cover," she warned playfully. Then she returned to her table, and Daniel returned to his book, but he could not stop thinking about the woman with the gentle smile and the honest eyes. He would learn her name soon enough, but for now, the moment felt complete in its quiet mystery.

The next time Daniel saw Elara was at the public library, three days later. He almost didn't recognize her at first because she was deep in concentration, her head bent over a stack of papers. She made several small sounds as she worked, the kind he was beginning to understand were involuntary. He hesitated near the entrance, debating whether to approach her. Eventually, curiosity and something deeper pulled him forward. He cleared his throat gently, and she looked up, recognition flickering across her face. "Coffee shop," she said, smiling. "The novel." Daniel nodded and sat across from her, though he hadn't planned to. He asked what she was working on, and she explained that she was studying to be a librarian, a dream she had carried since childhood. As they talked, Daniel noticed the various tics she experienced. Some were small, like a quick blink or a subtle head jerk. Others were vocal, little sounds that punctuated her sentences unexpectedly. She never drew attention to them, and he never did either. He simply listened, and she simply spoke. By the end of the afternoon, they had exchanged numbers. She told him her name was Elara, and he told her his was Daniel. She mentioned, almost casually, that she had Tourette syndrome, a neurological condition she had lived with since she was nine years old. She said it without shame and without apology. Daniel felt a swell of respect for her openness. He told her that he didn't mind at all, and he meant every word. As they parted ways outside the library, she laughed at something he said, and the sound was so genuine that it stayed with him long after she had walked away.

Section 3

Weeks turned into months, and Daniel and Elara's relationship deepened in ways neither of them had anticipated. They had long conversations about everything from books to politics to childhood memories. She told him about the difficult years in middle school, when classmates had teased her and teachers had misunderstood her condition. She told him about her parents, who had taken her to countless doctors before they finally received a proper diagnosis. She told him about the small victories, like the day she gave a presentation in college without letting her tics silence her. Daniel listened to every story with the same attention he gave to her words in the present. He learned which moments were harder for her, like when she was tired or stressed, and her tics would intensify. He learned how to be a calm presence during those times, offering her a steady hand or a quiet word. He never tried to fix her, because there was nothing to fix. He simply loved her for who she was. One evening, while they were cooking dinner together in his small kitchen, she had a particularly intense bout of motor tics. Her shoulder jerked sharply, and she knocked over a glass of water. She froze, her eyes filling with tears. Daniel knelt beside her, took her hand, and said, "It's okay, Elara. We've got this." She cried then, not from sadness, but from the overwhelming relief of being truly accepted. He held her until she was ready to stand, and together they cleaned up the mess, laughing softly at the absurdity of the moment. That night, Daniel realized he was in love with her, deeply and irrevocably. He had known it for a while, but in that quiet kitchen, with water still on the floor, the truth became undeniable.

Section 4

Daniel decided to propose on a Saturday in early autumn, when the leaves were turning gold and the air was crisp. He took Elara back to the coffee shop where they had first met, the same small place on Maple Street with its mismatched chairs and warm lighting. She recognized the significance of the location immediately and smiled at him with knowing eyes. He had planned a small speech, but when the moment came, he forgot every carefully prepared word. Instead, he spoke from his heart, telling her how she had changed his life simply by being herself. He told her that her courage inspired him every day. He told her that he wanted to be the steady hand by her side for the rest of their lives. He told her that he loved her laughter, her kindness, her intelligence, and yes, even the unexpected sounds she sometimes made, because they were part of the person he loved. As he spoke, Elara's eyes filled with tears, and she let out a small, joyful sound that was somewhere between a laugh and a gasp. She nodded before he even finished asking his question. He slipped the ring onto her finger, and she threw her arms around him, holding him close. The other customers in the shop began to clap, having witnessed the entire scene. Elara laughed, embarrassed but happy, and Daniel laughed with her, the sound of their joy filling the small space. Outside, the rain had stopped, and a faint rainbow arched over the city. As they walked home together, hand in hand, Daniel knew that their life would not always be easy. He knew there would be hard days and misunderstandings from strangers. But he also knew that he would face every challenge with her, because love, real love, was not about finding someone perfect. It was about finding someone whose imperfections became the most precious parts of who they were. And Elara, with all her complexity and her courage and her beautiful, honest heart, was exactly that person for him. They walked home slowly that evening, two people who had found each other against all odds, ready to build a life together one quiet, extraordinary day at a time.

"Laureates and Twins" is a remarkable documentary that will engage professionals in psychology from the opening frame to the closing credits. The film traces the intellectual lineages of Nobel laureates who shaped modern behavioral science while simultaneously examining how twin research illuminated the age old debate between nature and nurture.

The documentary excels in its biographical depth. It profiles laureates such as James Heckman Daniel Kahneman and Robert Shiller showing how their childhood curiosities evolved into rigorous academic inquiries. For psychologists these biographical segments provide valuable context for understanding how early life experiences shape scientific thinking. The narrative avoids hagiography and instead presents each laureate as a fallible human whose insights emerged through years of disciplined work.

What distinguishes this film from typical academic documentaries is its seamless integration of twin studies. The filmmakers use concordant and discordant monozygotic twin pairs to illustrate heritability estimates that range across traits like intelligence personality and vulnerability to depression. Viewers are introduced to the Minnesota Study of Twins Reared Apart and the work of researchers like Thomas Bouchard. The methodology sections are presented with enough rigor to satisfy researchers yet remain accessible enough for graduate students encountering these studies for the first time.

The cinematography of the twin interviews deserves particular praise. Observing identical twins interacting reveals subtle differences in mannerism and temperament that statistics alone cannot capture. The directors wisely resist the temptation to overplay the more sensational findings. Instead they present findings on cognitive decline and longevity with appropriate epistemic humility acknowledging methodological limitations such as small sample sizes and ascertainment bias.

For clinical psychologists the segments exploring genetic influence on treatment response are especially valuable. The film discusses how pharmacogenomic research using twin cohorts may eventually inform personalized treatment protocols for major depression and anxiety disorders. These discussions frame the ethical considerations thoughtfully and avoid deterministic implications.

The pacing is deliberate but never dull. Each chapter builds upon the previous one creating a coherent narrative arc. The film spans roughly ninety minutes and feels neither rushed nor padded. Sound design is unobtrusive and the archival footage from mid twentieth century research laboratories provides a fascinating glimpse into the evolution of research methodology.

The one minor criticism is that the documentary occasionally glosses over the contributions of researchers who were not selected for Nobel recognition. Scholars such as Sandra Scarr and Robert Plomin receive only brief mentions despite their foundational contributions to behavior genetics. A more inclusive treatment of these figures would have strengthened the historical narrative.

Overall "Laureates and Twins" is well worth watching for any psychologist seeking to understand the intellectual heritage of behavioral science and the continuing relevance of twin research. It works equally well as a teaching tool in graduate seminars or as enrichment viewing for seasoned practitioners. The film succeeds in honoring its subjects while advancing public understanding of complex research traditions.
